newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia National rail network sale clears hurdle.
newsitem.headline: Australia National rail network sale clears hurdle.

text.p: Legislation providing for the sale of the Australian National rail network has been passed by the South Australian legislative council, effectively clearing its last major hurdle, the State Government said on Wednesday.

The sale of AN, which operates freight services and workshops in South Australia and Tasmania plus three interstate passenger services, by the Australian government was dependent on enabling legislation being passed by South Australia.

Transport Minister Diana Laidlaw said in a statement the legislation would now go to the state's lower house where the government has the majority, unlike in the council where the Australian Democrats hold the balance of power.
The state legislation provides for the ownership of AN land, including track land, to be transferred to the state, separately from the owership of improvements by the private rail operators.
It also provides the transfer of the Leigh Creek-Port Augusta track, which carries coal to the Port Augusta power station, to the State government owned Optima Energy electricity generation arm.
Final bids for AN, which has attracted international interest, are due at the end of this month.
